- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust downward bias, especially after sharp spikes.
- After a strong upward spike (e.g., >75), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or apply decay to momentum.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 70–75 range after 76+), model often holds too high; apply downward bias or use 30-day moving average as anchor.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to adjust; trigger re-calibration if sentiment >0.67 after 5–7 days of low sentiment.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after day 10, reduce forecast growth rate by 10–20% for remaining days.
